ateret-zekenim/1:_: And women should not give garments to launderers after midday (Lechem Rav in the name of the pious Gaon Maharash in Mahari, of blessed memory); and one does not comfort a mourner on erev Pesach — I found written in Shulchan Aruch that our teacher the Gaon, may the memory of the holy be blessed, also [wrote that] taking nails is forbidden on erev Pesach after midday (Maharil). The custom is to get a haircut after midday through an akum, but not through a Jew — even for free it is forbidden (my teacher in Bach).
biur-halacha/1:_: From midday onwards — see Mishna Berurah; it is per the Yerushalmi the Poskim brought that the reason is because of Pesach slaughter; accordingly if Pesach falls on erev Shabbat, melacha is permitted by basic law until minchah since Pesach slaughter is the next day on Shabbat, as Maharil wrote; Rashi further explained lest he be preoccupied with melacha and forget his chametz removal, etc., and matzah preparation for the night, etc.; per this reason even when Pesach falls on erev Shabbat one should be careful not to do melacha from midday since he is preoccupied with chametz removal and matzah preparation for tomorrow's need; but most Poskim hold the Yerushalmi reason — therefore possibly there is no need to be stringent.
biur-halacha/4:א: (א) One who travels, etc. — see Mishna Berurah; know this entire seif is Rambam's language and Acharonim disputed his explanation; Magen Avraham and several Acharonim also hold like Tosafot and Rosh as Magen Avraham explained the entire seif — as we copied in Mishna Berurah; Shach's view in Yoreh De'ah end of siman 214 and so Chayei Adam and Gra hold Rambam has another view: per him one traveling from a place where they do to where they do not, without intention to return — nevertheless in the wilderness permitted; per them forbidden unless in the wilderness outside the city boundary; and with intention to return — per him permitted even in settlement if discreet; per them forbidden unless wilderness outside the city boundary; and one traveling from where they do not to where they do without intention to return — per him forbidden, must practice stringencies of place he left; per them permitted; nevertheless for practical law Shach wrote there and Chayei Adam and I saw in other Acharonim we follow Tosafot and Rosh as the Mechaber ruled in siman 496 and siman 474 and Yoreh De'ah siman 214 — therefore I explained the seif per Magen Avraham since at least for halacha we follow him even Shach and Chayei Adam.
biur-halacha/4:ב: (ב) And stringencies of the place, etc. — see Acharonim who wrote stringencies of the place he left do not cease from him only if the place he came to has a fixed custom of leniency; but not in a city without fixed custom. They also wrote in a community that was destroyed and resettled by others who practiced leniency in places they came from — they are not obligated now to be stringent though that destroyed settlement's people practiced stringency, since its people were dispersed their custom ceased; in Peri Megadim he doubts even if some remained since most were dispersed — see there; in my humble opinion if some remain, even a minority, all who come there are obligated to practice this place's custom, for there is no minimum for a community as Peri Chadash below proves; even many coming from outside attach to the minority there unless the new community practices separately and does not mix with the old — as in large communities with several kehillot each practicing ancestral custom; explained in Sefer Peri Chadash: a community with a minyan is called a community and arrivals attach; plainly his intent is it has all community needs as usual — synagogue, daily public prayer, rabbi, mikveh, etc.; otherwise it attaches to neighboring cities; see many details in Peri Chadash and Chayei Adam general rule 127.
biur-halacha/9:_: Dung in the courtyard one should not take out, etc. — see Biur Gra who wrote per Rambam this law applies only on Chol HaMoed, not on the fourteenth [even after midday] one takes to the garbage dump in all cases; per his words also for R' Chananel whose Gemara text reads thus. Know from Yerushalmi it is clear from a pen one certainly may take to the garbage dump; his words are brought in R' Chananel's explanation; whether Yerushalmi deals only on the fourteenth or even Chol HaMoed, on the fourteenth it is certainly permitted; it appears Bach was unaware of this Yerushalmi.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] On erev Pesach since, etc. Tosafot explained it is implied in the Yerushalmi that it is forbidden by Torah law and other Poskim dispute and say it is only rabbinic (Lechem Mishneh beginning of chapter "the place where they practiced").
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] [Levush] since each one, etc. Rashi there explained the reason: lest he be preoccupied with melacha and forget removal of chametz, slaughtering the Pesach, and preparing matzah, end of his words — implying he does not hold the sacrifice reason as Tosafot Yom Tov wrote there Mishnah 5; and it appears to me he proved thus: if he also held the sacrifice reason, Rashi should not have written the reason of Pesach slaughter and matzah preparation after midday, which is in any case forbidden because of the sacrifice — only the reason of his chametz removal alone, which also applies before midday where they practiced prohibition all day; however one may say he wrote because of erev Pesach falling on Shabbat that melacha is forbidden also on erev Shabbat from being preoccupied with the mitzvah; however where they practiced to do on erev Pesach until midday it appears permitted on erev Shabbat after midday even per Rashi, for he does not hold the preoccupation reason.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] [Levush] only he does not see, etc. But on erev Pesach we excommunicate and also he does not see a sign of blessing.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] Through a Samaritan, etc. And so they practiced to get a haircut through a Samaritan after midday, for through a Jew it is forbidden; and it is obvious a Jew is forbidden to cut hair for Samaritans. Maharil wrote in the gloss laws of Yom Tov not to cut nails from midday onwards, and its law is like all Chol HaMoed law, end of his words; and in Eliyah Zuta I wrote to permit if he forgot to cut before midday — see there. I further wrote that all those permitted to shave on Chol HaMoed as written in siman 471 — the same law permits on erev Pesach after midday; see R' Yosef Minz siman 4. Lechem Rav wrote in the name of his brother-in-law the Gaon Maharash that women should not give garments to a laundress after midday, end of his words; at first glance it appears permitted, for we hold like Rama that they practice melacha through akum after midday — why is giving to a laundress worse on erev Pesach after midday? Difficult to distinguish.
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: [5] To earn wages, etc. A worker who has nothing to eat is permitted — see siman 472.
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [6] Or for free, etc. In Eliyah Zuta I set a general rule: complete melacha even for free and for Yom Tov need is forbidden; but repair even for another is permitted for free for Yom Tov need; but for wages forbidden even for repair; and not for Yom Tov need — even repair for free forbidden.
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [7] [Levush] one who writes, etc. but for others even, etc. Rama did not write this; nevertheless it is reasonable as complete melacha forbidden even for mitzvah need; also difficult from siman 251 where he ruled specifically for wages forbidden but for free permitted for others since it is a mitzvah — and Tur's language there and here are identical; what appears to me: also wonder why Rama and Levush did not write above that complete melacha is forbidden even for free — it appears they hold Beit Yosef did not write thus only on erev Pesach where we find Mordechai holds so, but on erev Shabbat where we do not find Mordechai so — no distinction between repair and complete melacha, always permitted for free when for Shabbat or mitzvah need; the reason on erev Pesach where we excommunicate is stricter.
eliyah-rabbah/8:_: [8] Not to do, etc. And at night Beit Shammai forbid and Beit Hillel permit until sunrise (Mishnah chapter "the place where they practiced"); Bertinoro explained from the aspect of fasting that the day is forbidden in eating and the night permitted; Levush of Yom Tov wondered how melacha prohibition is derived from eating — see there where it is strained; I wonder more: on Taanis daf 12 the essence of rain fasts is not eating at night; and further wonder: they forbid melacha too, and by day specifically as the verse teaches there "sanctify a fast, call an assembly" — if so Bertinoro should have explained he learned melacha from melacha; and were it not for fear I would emend Bertinoro and in place of the word "eating" say "melacha" — all fits with heavenly assistance.
eliyah-rabbah/9:_: [9] [Levush] to settle, etc. Shach too agreed in Yoreh De'ah end of siman 214; and Lechem Mishneh explained chapter "the place where they practiced" that one traveling from abroad to Eretz Yisrael to settle practices leniency on second day Yom Tov of exile; these and other laws are explained in Eliyah Rabbah to Yoreh De'ah — see siman 496.
eliyah-rabbah/10:_: [10] [Levush] even to be lenient, etc. It implies if he cannot appear as though he has nothing to do, he is permitted to do melacha.
eshel-avraham/1:א: (א) From midday. For it is the time of slaughtering the Pesach; and even though now there is no Pesach, nevertheless it is a matter [prohibited] by vote — unlike uncovered water siman 116 — Rosh. And that it is not mentioned in Kol Bo is because of the daily offerings, for that is a communal sacrifice; and Rashi wrote the reason lest he delay chametz removal; practical difference: erev Pesach on Shabbat — Kaf HaChayyim.
eshel-avraham/1:ב: (ב) We excommunicate — all the more one strikes lashes of rebellion which is lighter than excommunication — see Kesubos 55 and Kiddushin 70 and Orach Chayyim siman 9; and also he does not see a sign of blessing from that melacha — see Rabbenu Nissim seif 2.
eshel-avraham/3:_: They do not do. In Jerusalem they practiced not to do; and it is obvious if it falls on Shabbat it is permitted on erev Shabbat — siman 9 seif 7.
eshel-avraham/4:א: (א) To a place. Sons of chutz la'aretz coming to Eretz Yisrael — may sons of Eretz Yisrael do melacha for them discreetly? See siman 9 and siman 10; and similarly may a kohen from Eretz Yisrael ascend to the duchan for them on second day Yom Tov — see siman 11.
eshel-avraham/4:ב: (ב) That he went there. A son of chutz la'aretz who comes to dwell in Eretz Yisrael and was not released, and before one Festival his intention is to return — must he observe second day Yom Tov? See siman 9 and siman 12; Maharival part 3 siman 93; and Yoreh De'ah siman 214. Rosh wondered: if they err thinking it forbidden we rule we tell them it is permitted; if prohibition is because of a fence, why mention erev Pesach even all year on erev Shabbat as a vow — see siman 214; it works out if they know it is permitted — only practical difference for those coming from other places who must practice stringency of the place they went to; Peri Chadash holds to strain — see there. Nevertheless Tosafot explain: a custom practiced as a fence, such as here — their children may not change their custom; but on other days of the year they may change — see Tosafot Pesachim daf 51. On this reasoning I compiled to answer Peri Chadash's difficulties: he wondered on Shulchan Aruch's contradictory words — Yoreh De'ah siman 228 wrote if it was with agreement as a fence for the public or safeguard, one may not permit, etc.; and further wrote: but a known permitted matter they were stringent as a safeguard — one does not permit automatically; he explains through regret and certainty one permits — see there; but truth guides otherwise after we find in the Gemara in Bishan they practiced not to go from Tyre to Sidon on Friday night — R' Yosi told them: your fathers could have done so; we cannot; you already accepted — hear, my son, your father's discipline, etc.; and Ran agreed that a matter ancestors practiced as prohibition and children thought it is forbidden by law — one reveals it is only a safeguard; per my view he wrote precisely: if with public fence agreement or safeguard — but when ancestors accepted, now children stand in their place for prohibition — do not abandon, etc. — one may not permit at all; unlike a known permitted matter one was stringent as safeguard alone — he alone was stringent, etc. — it is a vow and one permits through opening and regret; understand well.
eshel-avraham/5:א: (א) Not to do — and accordingly where they practiced to do, one may begin on the fourteenth and finish until midday — Kaf HaChayyim.
eshel-avraham/5:ב: (ב) For need. All the more when he has nothing to eat — Shulchan Aruch.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (a) [Seif 1] One who does melacha on erev Pesach from midday onwards, etc. — the reason is explained in the Yerushalmi: because it is the time of the Pesach offering from midday onwards; and on a day an individual brings a sacrifice melacha is forbidden; and what is not forbidden in melacha on erev Pesach except from midday onwards is because he may not offer it until midday; and even nowadays when there is no Pesach, since it was forbidden though the reason ceased the prohibition did not cease — Tosafot and Ran beginning of chapter "the place where they practiced"; and so Rosh there brought proof — see there; Beit Yosef, Beit David. However Rashi wrote the reason lest he be preoccupied with melacha and forget his chametz removal, Pesach slaughter, and matzah preparation for the night — see there; and though Rashi wrote this reason for those who practice not to do melacha all day, nevertheless there is a practical difference for erev Pesach on Shabbat: though there is no Pesach on erev Shabbat, melacha is forbidden that erev Shabbat for those who practice all day per Rashi's reason; but per Tosafot, Ran, and Rosh, since it is only because of the sacrifice and on erev Shabbat there is no sacrifice, it is permitted — as below letter 3 — see there. It appears from Beit Yosef he only brought Ran and Rosh who do not hold Rashi's reason; and so Levush only Tosafot and Ran's reason; and so Taz seif katan 2; Magen Avraham seif katan 1; and so Peri Chadash this reason is primary unlike Rashi — see there; and so Chok Yosef letter 1 this reason of Tosafot and Ran; Ma'amar Mordechai letter 1; Razah letter 1; Chayei Adam general rule 129 letter 2.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (b) And they wrote there Tosafot imply in the Yerushalmi it is forbidden by Torah law; and so Rosh in responsa general rule 55 siman 10; but Ran there wrote it is possible it is only rabbinic — see there; see Tosafot Chagigah 17b; and Maggid Mishneh laws of Temple vessels chapter 6 — Tosafot and Ran did not dispute except in explaining the Yerushalmi, but per our Gemara Tosafot too agree it is only rabbinic — see there; and so Rambam laws of Yom Tov chapter 8 law 18: the fourteenth of Nissan melacha is forbidden by rabbinic law like Chol HaMoed and it is lighter than Chol HaMoed, forbidden only from half the day onwards which is slaughter time; but from sunrise until half the day depends on custom — see there; and so Semag; and now too in our time it is forbidden on the sacrifice day by rabbinic law like Chol HaMoed — see there; and Peri Chadash decided melacha prohibition on erev Pesach after midday is only rabbinic per Rambam — see there; Shulchan Gavoah letter 1 wrote Rashi too holds only rabbinic; and so in Magen HaElef letter 3 it is only rabbinic.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: c) And when it came to pass on Shabbat, he wrote in the Sermons of the the Master the Great Shabbat, whoever wants to make it harder for himself not to do any work after midnight on the eve of that Shabbat, he will make it harder because he does not have a part of Yaush, and the Bedouin Preparatory 3 in his book Pesach Ma'ovin, O. 33, and wrote Da'in, this is nothing more than hardware, and he said, "Don't be careful about it, Efi, through the hardware of Yaush." The Po's agreed to the taste of a sacrifice, it seems simple in the name of the Yaush. And Rabbi Nachfa brought up the money of Chakh C. 7. The deen is permissible and it is complete, and the stricter Ta'ab of the Yaush. Who is the rabbi Admat Kodesh HA Chacha C. Yod Haela forbidding Ya'ush. It is true that the Rabbi O. A. wrote about the words of Adak Hanz Dain, his evidence is decisive at all, and he wrote mainly per the words of Nachafa in the Hanz money and per the words of the 3rd Hanz Yaush. And look at AR O. B. who wrote about the place where they used to do in the evening until midnight. Most of the PO's the reason for the prohibition is because of a sacrifice and even in places where they used to not do all day per the fact that it falls on Shabbat it is permissible to do work on the same day and in places where they used to do work until midnight even for Rashi it is permissible and the stricter MMM where they used to not do all day to feel according to Rashi Ta'ab.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: d) Name. From midnight and above, etc. Refer to Shekhna 3 C. 136 in the HGBI O. H. who wrote Daefi that the custom is in the after midnight not to engage in prakmatia them that I after midnight is prohibited from work on behalf of the offering of the Mashak sacrifice on Purim and with all this we have not seen or heard of anyone who fined someone who made goods in the after midnight at random and in Sinai Yaush. Who is the rabbi 24 B. Ramaj wrote a deshora per the ministers of Yaush and brought the zachal in this verse and wrote Danra that the rabbi did not see the words of the 13th Hanz Madla mentioned them. And he wrote that the Attorney General Dakan instituted in his city to close the shops at midnight and he also heard that the custom in Sufiya Yaa. And refer to l'fi da'at O. L. and above C. RNA O. B.
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (e) A worker who has nothing to eat on Pesach may do melacha on erev Pesach after midday, for it is no worse than Chol HaMoed called "mikra kodesh" — Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Beit Yosef letter 5; see there letter 2; Ateret Zekenim letter 5; Shulchan Gavoah letter 4; Chayei Adam letter 11; Peri Chadash seif 5; Chok Yosef letter 8; Chayei Adam general rule 129 letter 4; Ruach Chayim letter 3; Mishna Berurah letter 6; see below letter 21 and siman 472 seif 2 and siman 475 seif 3.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (f) There — we excommunicate him. One need not say we strike lashes of rebellion if he was not excommunicated — Rambam laws of Yom Tov chapter 8 law 17; the reason Magen Mishneh wrote excommunication is more severe than rebuke as explained in chapter 1 — see there; and so Tosafot Kesubos 28a; and Rashi Kiddushin 70b; Beit David, Kaf HaChayyim letter 2 — see there; for a Torah scholar we only strike discreetly — Shulchan Gavoah letter 1 and this is Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 334 seif 42 — see there; see below siman 496 seif 1 and responsum Sha'ar Efrayim siman 64 on not excommunicating a Torah scholar — see there; see below siman 476 letter 11.
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (g) There — we excommunicate him. They were stricter on this than other eves of Festivals and Shabbat where we only say from minchah onwards he does not see a sign of blessing in that melacha, but we do not excommunicate; but on erev Pesach from midday onwards we also excommunicate — see there letter 1 and this is from the Gemara Pesachim 50b; see above siman 251 letter 5.
kaf-hachayyim/8:_: (h) There — we excommunicate him. Tur brings the Gemara: he does not see a sign of blessing forever; Ra'avan and Rashi explained specifically in that matter; "forever" means even if he has profit from it he loses correspondingly from another place — Beit David, Bach, Taz seif katan 1; Kaf HaChayyim letter 3; and so Acharonim; implied from Rambam laws of Yom Tov chapter 8 law 17 there is also prohibition; and so Kaf HaChayyim there; Peri Chadash in siman 496 letter 18; Shulchan Gavoah siman 251 letter 1; see above siman 251 letter 7.
kaf-hachayyim/9:_: (i) There — even to do for free is forbidden. If it is complete melacha as below seif 2 in the gloss — see there; however to wash after midday is permitted — Magen Tzedek siman 465; and so in derashot Maharil Shabbat Hagadol in the gloss.
kaf-hachayyim/10:_: (j) There — and there is one who forbids even through akum. Like melacha of Chol HaMoed — Beit Yosef in the name of Mordechai; see below siman 473.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Mishna Berurah note 1 (Tosafot and Ran) — see in Sefer Tosafot Shabbat siman 244:63.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: See Magen Avraham and Peri Chadash.
yad-ephraim/1:_: See Magen Avraham seif katan 13 and Eliyah Rabbah.
